patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient comes in for a routine checkup without any specific complaints. He maintains an active lifestyle with jogging and gardening. He has been retired since age 50 and enjoys spending his mornings in the park and afternoons in his garden.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Presence of a lesion on the scalp

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: No history of smoking. Drinks alcohol occasionally.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies any symptoms of fatigue, weight loss, fever, or other systemic symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Perform a routine checkup on a 68-year-old man, assess any dermatological findings, and formulate a diagnosis.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hello doctor—I'm here for a routine checkup. I’m generally doing well, staying active with jogging and gardening, but I’ve noticed a lesion on my scalp that brought me in.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any change in the shape or contour of either breast—such as one breast looking different from before, a new dimpling, or a change in how it sits? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No, doctor—I've not noticed any changes to either breast, and I’m not experiencing any breast-related symptoms. My main concern is the lesion on my scalp that led me to come in.

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **Are you having any abdominal pain right now?**
turns.patient_answer: No, doctor—I’m not having any abdominal pain. I feel generally well otherwise.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or run-down more than usual lately (for example, lacking energy or feeling unusually tired)?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t been feeling weak or run-down more than usual, and I haven’t noticed any unusual tiredness.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had diarrhea recently—meaning loose or watery stools more than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t had diarrhea or any change in my stool; everything’s been normal as far as I can tell. I’m feeling well overall, just concerned about the lesion on my scalp that I noticed.”

turns.doctor_question: Are you having **profuse sweating**—like sweating a lot even when you’re not doing much, or soaking through clothes or bedding?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I’m not having profuse sweating. I’ve been feeling well overall, and I’m only concerned about the lesion on my scalp.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have pain in your wrist (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I’m not having any wrist pain right now. I’ve been feeling well overall, aside from the lesion on my scalp that I came in to have checked.”

turns.doctor_question: When you wake up in the morning, do you feel stiffness in your joints or muscles that lasts **more than 30 minutes** before it starts to ease? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—when I wake up I don’t have joint or muscle stiffness that lasts more than 30 minutes; it eases fairly quickly. I’m otherwise feeling well and it’s mainly the scalp lesion that I’m concerned about.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a breast lump or mass that feels **fixed in place**—meaning it doesn’t move much when you gently press it? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any breast lump or mass, and nothing is fixed or changing in either breast. My concern is still the lesion on my scalp that brought me in.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have any pain in your knee (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I’m not having any knee pain. I’m feeling well overall; my only concern remains the lesion on my scalp.”

turns.doctor_question: When you walk, do you get pain or cramping in your calf that improves or goes away when you stop and rest? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I'm not getting any calf pain or cramping when I walk, and it doesn’t improve with rest because it isn’t happening. I feel well overall; my only concern is the lesion on my scalp.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a **firm or hard lump/mass in your thigh** (that feels more solid than the surrounding tissue)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any firm or hard lump in my thigh. I’m otherwise feeling well and my only concern is still the lesion on my scalp.”
